description: Pure policy unit (extend packages/auth/src/lib/authPolicy.test.ts): normalize maps absent/non-array to null and filters+dedupes+orders arrays; applyPolicyChange keeps the previous list on undefined and replaces on explicit []; validatePolicyChange rejects ['google','okta'] with client_portal_sso_provider_invalid; offeredClientPortalSsoProviders returns available for null, the intersection for ['azure-ad'], and [] for [].

Availability matrix unit (extend packages/auth/src/lib/sso/clientPortalSsoResolution.test.ts, credential helpers and policy loader mocked): EE with app Google+Microsoft and no policy offers both; tenant-only Keycloak realm is offered; policy ['azure-ad'] offers only azure-ad even though Google app creds exist; CE offers [].

DB-backed integration (server/src/test/integration, real tenant_settings + audit_logs): happy path - saveTenantAuthPolicy with clientPortalSsoProviders ['azure-ad'] persists under settings.sso without dropping other sso keys (e.g. autoLinkClient), writes a LOGIN_POLICY_CHANGED row whose after contains the list, and loadTenantAuthPolicy round-trips it; guard path - an update carrying an unsupported id is rejected by validatePolicyChange and tenant_settings is unchanged.

SsoProviderButtons component (jsdom, EE edition): authSurface client_portal with offeredProviders ['azure-ad'] renders only the Microsoft button on first render and never fetches /api/auth/providers; offeredProviders [] renders nothing; omitting the prop on the MSP surface still renders the registry-driven set (regression).

LoginPolicySettings component (jsdom, actions mocked, alongside loginPolicySettings.staleBreakGlass.test.tsx): with availableClientPortalSsoProviders [google, azure-ad] and a null list both boxes are checked; unchecking Google calls updateLoginPolicyAction with { clientPortalSsoProviders: ['azure-ad'] }; a failed save reverts the checkbox and shows the error alert; an empty available list shows the none-available note.

Edition wiring: editionSwapping.test.ts asserts @alga-psa/auth/sso/entry resolves to packages/auth/src/components/SsoProviderButtons.tsx for both CE and EE webpack configs, and ssoProviderEditionGate.unit.test.tsx keeps the CE (Keycloak on MSP, nothing on client portal) / EE (all three) gate using the single component.
